AWPTCM-T33237.objective:
• Fiber monitoring is disabled by default on all ports.
  • Fiber monitoring can be enabled and subsequently disabled on supported ports with compliant DDM pluggables.
  • Fiber monitoring can only be configured on provisioned ports; attempts on unsupported or non-provisioned ports are rejected or logged.
  • The "show system fiber-monitoring" command accurately reports the enabled state, configured sensitivity, moving average baseline, and current pluggable readings.
  • Log messages are generated when received optical power falls below the configured threshold or when an unsupported module is inserted on a monitored port.
  • Fiber monitoring configuration and status are included in tech support output.
  • Debug commands for fiber monitoring function correctly and do not appear in the running configuration.
  • Non-AT hardware and non-DDM pluggables are correctly identified and handled (rejection or appropriate logging).

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability
Verify that fiber monitoring is disabled by default. Enable fiber monitoring on a supported port with a compliant DDM pluggable and confirm it can be disabled again.
Attempt to configure fiber monitoring on a non-provisioned or unsupported port. Confirm the configuration is rejected or an appropriate log message is generated.
Configure fiber monitoring with different sensitivity levels and moving average periods. Verify that "show system fiber-monitoring" accurately reflects the configured values and current readings.
Trigger threshold breach (low received power) and unsupported module insertion. Confirm log messages are generated as expected.
Verify that fiber monitoring configuration and status appear in tech support output.
Test debug commands for fiber monitoring. Confirm they function and are not written to the running configuration.
Test with non-AT hardware and non-DDM pluggables. Confirm correct identification, rejection, or logging behavior.
